No schema migration, dependency addition, package install, push, deploy, live scheduled-task operation or automatic Git reset. Work only in the assigned worktree. Interfaces: Produce PROTOCOL=1, RUN_FORMAT=1; validate_record(kind: str, value: dict) -> dict; atomic_json(path: Path, value: dict) -> None; Journal(root: Path).append(kind: str, data: dict) -> dict and .replay(after: int) -> list[dict]. Produce ActivityBarrier with try_enter(kind: str, *, control: bool=False) -> context-manager-or-None, close(generation: int) -> None, seal(generation: int) -> None, reopen(generation: int) -> None, snapshot() -> dict. A returned section counts immediately, before __enter__; __exit__ always releases. Snapshot has generation, closed, sealed, active_sections and counts by kind. close denies work; counted control=True sections may enter until seal denies all admission. Matching reopen unseals. Admission close and section acquisition share one mutex. The module runs standalone with only stdlib imports.

Work: Implement the protocol records and enums from the design, strict full lowercase 40-hex SHAs and increasing generations/sequences. Journal append uses one immutable sequence file per event before replacing state; recover a complete journal record whose state update was interrupted. Exclude partial files, detect gaps/corruption, and block unknown versions. Child and parent writers never overwrite each other's records. Atomic writes flush and fsync before replace. An installer-supplied state root carries owner ACLs; never log secrets. A stale generation cannot reopen a current barrier. This foundational module must import without FastAPI or the drover package.

Verification: run the focused test tests.test_reload_protocol using the preinstalled interpreter; new platform-independent tests must execute, not skip. Required Windows-only checks need an authorized Windows worker and an actual passing receipt. See the implementation plan task #0 for test steps.
acceptance: Barrier close races atomically with acquisition; an already acquired section can finish, and all later acquisition is denied until matching reopen.
Torn state after durable journal append replays exactly once; malformed/gapped/unknown-version data fails closed without changing active SHA.
Record validation covers every field in the spec worked example; journal event IDs support transactional ledger mirroring deduplication.

Interfaces: Consume protocol records. Produce transition(state: dict, event: dict, now: float) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]: a pure reducer returning next state and ordered effect descriptions. Work: Define idle/pending/draining/stopping/validating/committed and blocked/rolling_back/rolled_back/failed transitions exactly as the design. One fallback only; two attempts per ten minutes including fallback, persisted failed latch survives scheduled-task relaunch. Only healthy candidate commit changes active/previous. Fallback disables auto and keeps admission closed; cancel then explicitly resumes it. Distinguish intentional exit 75, owner stop, unexpected exit and identity uncertainty. Stale events cannot change state.
